title: Beyond Behavioral Accuracy: Evaluating Individual-Level Fidelity in LLM Investor Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2610.26524v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as user simulators, but can they faithfully reproduce an individual's behavior and decision logic over time? We investigate this question in a longitudinal paper-trading study with 80 participants. Using rolling next-day predictions, we evaluate trading activity, buy-sell structure, asset selection, and portfolio outcomes, complemented by controlled input ablations and participant-rated explanation alignment. No evaluated LLM reliably outperforms a simple recent-activity persistence baseline for predicting trade occurrence, while buy-sell structure and asset selection remain difficult to reproduce. Similar activity-level performance can also yield substantially different portfolio trajectories. translated_title: 超越行为准确性：评估大语言模型投资者模拟中的个体层面保真度
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用作用户模拟器，但它们能否随时间推移忠实地再现个体的行为和决策逻辑？我们通过一项涉及80名参与者的纵向模拟交易（paper-trading）研究来探讨这一问题。通过滚动式次日预测，我们评估了交易活动、买卖结构、资产选择和投资组合结果，并辅以受控输入消融实验和参与者评分的解释一致性评估。在预测交易发生方面，没有任何被评估的LLM能够可靠地超越简单的近期活动持续性基线，而买卖结构和资产选择仍然难以复现。相似的活动层面表现也可能产生截然不同的投资组合轨迹。消融实验表明，活动预测主要依赖于近期交易，而资产选择则对多个证据来源敏感。参与者认为解释与……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过80名参与者的纵向模拟交易实验，首次系统评估了LLM在个体层面对投资者行为与决策逻辑的保真度，发现当前LLM无法超越简单基线，买卖结构与资产选择尤其难以复现，且相似的活动表现会导致截然不同的投资组合轨迹。
en_tdlr: Through a longitudinal paper-trading study with 80 participants, this work systematically evaluates individual-level fidelity of LLM investor simulation, showing that current LLMs fail to outperform a simple persistence baseline, struggle to reproduce buy-sell structure and asset selection, and that similar activity-level performance can lead to substantially different portfolio trajectories.
